column1: # tests/mutants/pre-pr-gate-subagent.tsv — single-clause mutants of tools/pre-pr-gate.sh's subagent git floor, slices 1-2:
# the reader half check_subgit / sg_path / sg_cd (dir #675 B9-B12, dir #790) and the shell half sg_val .. sg_check (dir #911).
# keel-self-maintenance: read by tools/self/mutation-sweep.sh (swept against tests/test_pre_pr_gate_subagent_floor.sh)
# and checked for staleness by tests/test_mutation_lists.sh.
# Columns, TAB-separated: id, file, needle, replacement, note — the format tests/mutants/pre-pr-gate.tsv documents.
# - `w_plain` on the verb word (`if (j > ntok || !w_plain(j)) return`) and on the word after `builtin`: an expansion
#   keeps its `$` source text, so such a word can never equal a mutating verb or cd, pushd, popd; dropping either
# - `unset CDPATH;` in `sg_gitdir_common`: its argument is always absolute (an absolute member joined with the path,
#   or the path itself), and `git --git-dir=<absolute> rev-parse --git-common-dir` answers an absolute path
#   (measured for a `.git` dir, a linked worktree's gitfile and its `.git/worktrees/<x>` dir, git 2.52), so the
#   `cd` never consults CDPATH — unlike `sg_common_dir`, whose relative answer SW08 pins.
# - `sg_apply_cd`'s pending targets (`pend[...]="$t"`) and the cap of 8 that bounds only them: a pending target is
#   a path that is not a directory when the hook runs, every later relative join through it names a missing path,
#   an absolute one is reached from the real member that a failed cd keeps beside it, so no pending member can
#   ever be a hit; dropping either is equivalent as the code stands.
# Not yet covered (a later slice, dir #912): the verb classification sg_mut and sg_valopt.
